title: $\gamma$-weakly $\theta$-up-concavity: A Unified Framework for Non-Convex Optimization Beyond DR-Submodular and OSS Functions
claim: Existing function classes are nested inside one broader unified class, and this map shows how they relate by inclusion.
layout: 2 rows, left-to-right flow, boxed class nodes joined by arrows
description: A flow diagram of rounded boxes joined by arrows, showing how function classes relate. The top row runs left to right: C² ∩ F₁^DR, then F_γ^DR, then F_γ, then F_{γ,1,σ}, and finally F_{γ,θ}. F_{γ,θ} is the only box with a blue fill, and it marks the most general class. The bottom row starts with F₀^OSS = C² ∩ F₁ and continues through C² ∩ F_{1,1,σ/2} and F^OSS_{σ/2} to F_{1,1,σ}. Cross links join the rows. An arrow runs down from C² ∩ F₁^DR to F₀^OSS. Another runs from F₀^OSS up to F_γ. A third runs up from F_{1,1,σ} to F_{γ,1,σ}. The boxes are pale yellow and the text is black, with no other decoration. The eye lands first on the blue box at the far right.
caption: Containment relations among the function classes introduced in Section 3. An arrow A →B indicates that A ⊆B. The arrow into Fγ,θ means that Fγ,1,σ is the special case θ(x) = ∥x∥σ
abstract: Many objectives in machine learning and combinatorial optimization are non-concave. We introduce $Î³$-weak $Î¸$-up-concavity, a first-order condition for nonnegative monotone functions in which a scaling function $Î¸$ lets the curvature change with the size of the solution. The resulting class strictly contains monotone DR-submodular functions and One-Sided Smooth (OSS) functions. It also contains functions whose marginal gains first increase and then decrease, and functions that vanish faster than any power of the norm at the origin. We construct a surrogate gradient from gradients along the segment from the origin to the current point and prove an upper-linearization inequality with a point-dependent approximation coefficient. Restricting actions to the closed convex hull of the coordinate-wise maximal feasible points makes this coefficient uniformly positive, with a value determined by the curvature parameters and the geometry of the feasible set. Standard reductions to linear optimization then give offline approximation algorithms and online algorithms with regret guarantees. The coefficient matches the optimal one for DR-submodular maximization and improves the best known coefficients for OSS maximization over matroid constraints whenever the OSS parameter is positive.
